options: One row per cached compiled plan, including usecounts, object type, and size
Backup history, not query plans
Index fragmentation levels
Only currently executing queries, not cached plans
questions.explain: sys.dm_exec_cached_plans exposes the plan cache directly, with usecounts showing how often each plan has been reused.

questions.q: What causes ad hoc plan bloat?
options: Rebuilding indexes too frequently
An application building SQL as a literal string with values baked in, so every distinct literal produces a cache miss and a brand-new plan
Setting max server memory too high
Using stored procedures too often
questions.explain: Unparameterized literal SQL means each call has different query text, forcing a fresh compile and cache entry every time.

questions.q: What is the real fix for ad hoc plan bloat, versus what optimize for ad hoc workloads does?
options: There is no fix — ad hoc bloat is unavoidable
optimize for ad hoc workloads is itself the complete fix
Rebooting the SQL Server service is the fix
The real fix is parameterizing the application (e.g. sp_executesql); optimize for ad hoc workloads only mitigates the damage by caching a lightweight stub first
questions.explain: The setting reduces wasted cache memory but doesn't stop the bloat — proper parameterization is the actual fix.

questions.q: What does a large number of rows with usecounts = 1 and near-identical text differing only by a literal value indicate?
options: A healthy, well-parameterized workload
The signature of ad hoc plan bloat
A backup failure
An index fragmentation problem
questions.explain: This exact pattern — one-off plans differing only by a literal — is how you spot ad hoc bloat in the cache.

questions.q: In a healthy OLTP workload's plan cache, what should usecounts typically look like?
options: Usecounts should always be 0
Well above 1 for most plans, since parameterized queries and stored procedures reuse the same compiled plan repeatedly
Always exactly 1 for every plan
Usecounts has no relationship to workload health
questions.explain: Plan reuse — the point of the cache — shows up as usecounts well above 1 for the queries actually running repeatedly.
